run.narrative_md:
**Run c33f62a1d521 (2026-10-12) — milestone 5, speed.**

The run stopped on an empty graft, and here that is the honest result: the build from milestone 4 already met the speed target, so neither variant had anything to change.

Both variants ran one after the other, made no commits, and passed the cumulative gate. The measured 95th-percentile click-to-paint under the 4× CPU slowdown was 16.5 ms for variant 1 and 17.8 ms for variant 2, against a target of 100 ms. Because neither changed any code, the two readings are two measurements of the same build, and the difference between them is measurement noise, not a difference between approaches. The approaches the variants were assigned (deferring writes off the interaction; moving sync into a Web Worker) were not built.

One risk is deferred to the operator: the figure comes from headless Chromium on a laptop under an artificial slowdown. It is a comparison instrument and not a prediction of the learner's phone.

Next: the operator decides the boundary (`approve-boundary learn-anywhere 5 --proceed --accept-risk 0`). That is the last milestone.
